answer: Pay identities as a mesa pays lookouts: one reward per uncorrelated watch. Throughout the epoch, random alarms ring at unpredictable minutes; each agent must answer from its post within seconds. A lone agent easily keeps its watch. A sybil herd shares one operator, one host and one sleep cycle, so its members miss, wake and lag together — their failures bend like one plume in a gale. The ledger groups near-perfectly correlated responders and pays the cluster once, so cloning adds exposure to detection, not rewards.
